correctness.rationale: For every selected set of k nonoverlapping cyclic-adjacent edges, its prescribed-chord probability is (2n-2k-1)!!/(2n-1)!! and deleting it preserves the cyclic order and all crossings of residual chords. Summation over the m_{n,k}=2n/(2n-k) binomial(2n-k,k) cycle-edge matchings proves the exact mixed factorial identity. Setting k=1 and 2 and using Flajolet–Noy Theorem 3 yields Cov(X,S)=-2n(n-1)/(3(2n-1)) and Corr(X,S)=-sqrt(5/(n+3)). Fixed-k conditional CLTs combined with factorial bounds c_{n,k}<=4/(3k!) rigorously justify dominated convergence for the joint transform. An independently implemented exhaustive enumerator checked all matching cases n=2,...,7 and 494 exact rational assertions. The crossing CLT is explicitly imported; finite checks are not claimed as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The new claim is an exact mixed crossing/simple-chord factorial identity with full bivariate generating law, sharp finite negative correlation and joint independent Gaussian–Poisson limit. Paguyo (2021) treats the same pair but proves only separate approximations; Flajolet–Noy (2000) covers crossings alone; Acan (2017) covers other short-chord and graph statistics; Young (2020) covers linear short chords. Their inspected statements and implications do not determine the mixed law. Broad searches and mathematical-record comparisons found no equivalent; residual historical-priority risk remains.

value.rationale: Paguyo’s pair of natural observables are both studied in the same random diagram, yet separate normal and Poisson limit statements do not establish their asymptotic independence. The exact all-n factorial deletion identity structurally resolves their full finite dependence, produces the unexpectedly elementary correlation -sqrt(5/(n+3)), and proves the product limit without an unproved independence assumption. The result is a motivated complete bivariate law rather than a routine marginal formula or isolated low-order computation.
